title: Finalizers
sub: A last resort you can't rely on
cards/0/title: A finalizer is a last resort
cards/0/body:
A class can declare a finalizer, ~Name(). The GC calls it before freeing the object's memory.

It was invented for things the GC doesn't know about: file handles, sockets, OS memory.
cards/1/body:
An object with a finalizer can't be removed right away. The GC puts it on the finalization queue, a separate thread calls the finalizer at some later point, and only the next collection frees the memory.

The object lives longer and has time to get promoted to an older generation.
cards/2/task: Clear both references and make sure F is really removed. Count how many steps it took.
cards/3/q: How many garbage collections does it take to free the memory of an object with a finalizer?
cards/3/options/0: At least two: the first queues it, the second frees it
cards/3/options/2: None: the finalizer frees the memory itself
cards/3/explain: The first collection finds the object and queues it. The finalizer runs. The next collection of its generation frees the memory.
cards/4/options/0: Unknown: once the GC finds the object and the finalizer thread gets to it
cards/4/explain: The timing isn't guaranteed: maybe in a millisecond, maybe in a minute.
cards/5/title: What you can't trust a finalizer with
cards/5/body:
The timing isn't guaranteed.
The order between objects isn't guaranteed: a neighboring object may already be finalized.
In .NET Core and .NET 5+, finalizers aren't run at all when the program exits.

A file that only the finalizer closes may never be fully written.
cards/6/q: What is true about finalizers? Select all that apply.
cards/6/options/0: An object with a finalizer lives longer
cards/6/options/1: The order of calls between objects isn't guaranteed
cards/6/options/2: They run on a separate thread
cards/6/options/3: They run the instant an object becomes garbage
cards/6/options/4: In .NET 8 they're guaranteed to run on program exit
cards/6/explain: A finalizer is a backup mechanism. For timely cleanup there's Dispose, the next lesson.
cards/7/q: Which line in this finalizer is dangerous?
cards/7/explain: _writer is another managed object. By the time ~Logger runs, it may already be finalized and closed. A finalizer should touch only unmanaged resources.
cards/8/q: A regular class with no native resources. Does it need a finalizer?
cards/8/options/0: No: it would only slow collection down
cards/8/options/2: Yes, otherwise the memory won't be freed
cards/8/explain: The GC frees managed memory on its own. An unneeded finalizer means an extra queue and an extra collection.
